findings.title: `prisma` used without being imported
findings.body: `getClient` now calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` but the file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` (imports only include jsforce, rrule, zod, lib helpers and types). This is a TypeScript compile error and, if it slipped through, a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime, which would break every Salesforce calendar operation since `getClient` runs in the constructor.

findings.title: Freshly refreshed Salesforce token is persisted but the stale token is used for the connection
findings.body: After refreshing the access token and writing `accessTokenParsed.data` to the DB, the jsforce Connection is still constructed with `credentialKey.access_token` / `credentialKey.instance_url` from the old credential. The new access token is never used in-process, so if the old one was expired the connection still fails. Additionally `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure, so the `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is dead, and `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable (HTTP/2 responses have an empty statusText), which would spuriously throw a 400 for successful refreshes. The refresh also now happens unconditionally on every service instantiation instead of only when the token is expired.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses nonsensical computed keys, so sync-mode parsing always fails
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates `ZodString.toString()` which yields the string "[object Object]" as the property name. The resulting schema is `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": number }` (the second computed key overwrites the first with `z.unknown().optional()`, or vice versa). It does not express "any numeric property is the expiry" at all. Depending on evaluation order the schema either requires a literal `"[object Object]"` number field (all real responses fail → `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`), or is just `{access_token}` with every other field stripped by zod's default strip behaviour, dropping `expires_in`/`expiry_date` entirely. Either way, when `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set the token refresh for Google, Office365, Zoom and Salesforce is broken.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token "refresh_token" is injected and can overwrite the real refresh token in the DB
findings.body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper mutates `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. This runs in both sync and non-sync modes. In Office365 (`refresh_token` is `.optional()` in its schema) the result is spread over the stored credential (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`), so whenever Microsoft omits the refresh token the real one is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token" and persisted, permanently breaking future refreshes for that user. In Zoom the same value is written to `key.refresh_token`. The placeholder should never be written over an existing valid token.

findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse result object instead of the credential data
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the credential object directly. Now `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` persists `{success: true, data: {...}}` as the credential key. On the next load `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails because `access_token`/`refresh_token` are nested under `data`, so every Google Calendar credential that goes through a refresh becomes unusable. Should be `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data`.

findings.title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response regardless of what the wrapped refresh function returns
findings.body: Callers treat the return value of `refreshOAuthTokens` as whatever their own `refreshFunction` returns: Google expects a Gaxios response and reads `res.data`; HubSpot expects a `HubspotToken` object and reads `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` and stores it as the DB key; Zoho CRM / Zoho Bigin expect an axios response and read `.data`. When credential sync is enabled the helper instead returns a WHATWG `Response`, so `res.data` is `undefined` (Google crashes on `token.access_token`), HubSpot computes `NaN` expiry and persists a serialized `Response` (`{}`) as the credential key, and Zoho reads `undefined.error` and throws. Only the fetch-based adapters (O365, Zoom, Webex, Lark) can work in sync mode. The helper must normalize the sync response into the shape each adapter expects (or adapters must handle both).

findings.title: Call to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication
findings.body: The POST to the self-hoster's sync endpoint sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret, signature or bearer header. The endpoint is expected to return live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs, so anyone who can reach it can harvest every user's third-party tokens by iterating IDs. Cal.com already has `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` for the reverse direction; the outbound request should at least include it (e.g. in the configured header) so the receiving side can authenticate the caller.

findings.title: credentialId passed where userId is expected
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id as the `userId` argument. In sync mode this sends the wrong `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint (and would wrongly trigger sync for team credentials that have no user). `biginAuth` has access to `credential.userId`; it should be threaded through and used here.

findings.title: In sync mode the O365 expires_in transform is bypassed, so the token is treated as always expired
findings.body: `refreshTokenResponseSchema` converts the relative `expires_in` seconds into an absolute epoch timestamp, and `getToken` compares that against now via `isExpired(o365AuthCredentials.expires_in)`. When sync is enabled `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead, which (if it parses at all) leaves `expires_in` as a small relative number (e.g. 3600). `isExpired(3600)` is always true, so every Graph call triggers a new round-trip to the sync endpoint and a DB write, and the useful error logging that was removed in this diff no longer surfaces malformed responses.

findings.title: Unvalidated input paths produce unhandled 500s and no method restriction
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on bad input, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a bad ciphertext or when `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is empty, and the handler accepts any HTTP method (a GET with no body reaches `.parse(undefined)`). None of these are caught, so the caller gets a generic Next.js 500 with no actionable message. Use `safeParse`, wrap decryption in try/catch returning 400, and reject non-POST requests. Also the secret comparison uses `!==` rather than a constant-time compare (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`), which is the norm for webhook secrets.

findings.title: Decrypted payload is stored as the credential key without validation
findings.body: `keys` is whatever `JSON.parse` returns (could be a string, number, null or array) and is written directly to `credential.key`. A malformed or non-object payload would create a credential that every CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter fails to parse, and the existing `invalid` flag is never reset to `false` when a credential is overwritten with fresh keys, so a previously invalidated credential stays marked invalid even after a successful sync.

findings.title: No tests for the new shared OAuth helpers or webhook endpoint
findings.body: The PR introduces shared logic (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`) that is now on the token-refresh path of ~10 integrations, plus a new unauthenticated-by-env webhook that writes credentials. The author notes no tests were added. Given the schema-construction bug and the return-shape mismatch above, unit tests for both sync and non-sync branches (and for the webhook's auth / validation / upsert paths) would have caught these before merge.
